hero.heading: Register as Self-Employed in Malta
hero.subtext: Step-by-step guide to starting your freelance or business activity

steps.heading: 4 steps to become self-employed
steps.description: Follow these official steps to legally register your self-employment in Malta.

ssn.title: Get your Social Security Number
ssn.description: Required to pay contributions and register as self-employed. Apply at the Social Security office in Malta.

jobsplus.title: Register with Jobsplus
jobsplus.description: Submit the self-employment engagement form online via the Jobsplus portal. This is the main mandatory step.

tax.title: Register for Tax
tax.description: Obtain your tax number from the Malta Tax and Customs Administration and prepare for annual income tax returns.

vat.title: Register for VAT (if required)
vat.description: Required if your annual turnover exceeds the VAT threshold. Depends on your business activity and income.

requirements.heading: Requirements to register
requirements.description: Make sure you have the following before starting the registration process.
items: Valid ID card or residence permit
Social Security Number (if not yet assigned)
VAT registration (if your income exceeds the threshold)
Maltese bank account for tax payments

items.title: Income tax applies
items.description: You must file an annual income tax return. Malta uses progressive brackets starting from 0% on the first €12,000.

items.title: Social security contributions
items.description: Self-employed individuals pay Class 2 contributions — 15% of net taxable income. Payable to the Social Security office.

items.title: VAT depends on your income
items.description: VAT registration is required once your annual turnover exceeds the applicable threshold for your business category.

cta.heading: Start your self-employment journey
cta.subtext: Register officially with Jobsplus and get your tax number today.

hero.heading: Tax Calculator for Self-Employed
hero.subtext: Estimate your annual income tax and social security contributions based on Malta tax law 2026. Progressive brackets, self-employed regime.

form.title: Your income details
form.partTimeDesc: 10% flat rate on income up to €12,000

result.title: Your tax estimate
result.placeholder: Enter your income above to see your estimate

insights.belowThreshold: Your income falls within the 0% tax bracket — no income tax is due in Malta below €12,000.
insights.sscRequired: Social Security contributions (Class 2, 15%) are mandatory for all self-employed individuals in Malta.
insights.partTimeRegime: Your income is taxed under the part-time flat rate of 10%, applied on income up to €12,000.
insights.multipleBrackets: Your income is taxed progressively — each portion falls into its applicable bracket and is taxed at that rate only.

items.title: Progressive Income Tax
items.desc: Malta applies four brackets: 0% on the first €12,000, 15% on €12,001–€16,000, 25% on €16,001–€60,000, and 35% above €60,000. Only the slice of income in each bracket is taxed at that rate.

items.title: Social Security — Class 2
items.desc: As a self-employed individual, 15% of your taxable income is paid to the Social Security Department as Class 2 contributions. No annual cap applies.

items.title: Part-time Regime
items.desc: If you selected part-time, a flat 10% rate was applied on income up to €12,000 instead of the progressive brackets.
